item.title: Cornell rape lawsuit takes new turn as defendant seeks gag order
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Lawyers for one of the men named in a civil lawsuit brought by a former Cornell University student who alleged she was sexually assaulted at a school fraternity in 2024 is asking a New York judge to impose a gag order in the case, arguing the publicity surrounding the case risks tainting potential jurors. Attorneys for Diego Sarabia on Monday asked for "narrowly tailored restrictions" that would prevent lawyers and parties in the civil case from commenting on the allegations outside of court. "Since this action began, Plaintiff's counsel has repeatedly addressed the merits through widely disseminated media statements," the motion said. "These statements present disputed allegations and interpretations of evidence to the public before discovery and trial." Attorney says Jane Doe facing threats, calls out alleged 'failures' of Cornell, law enforcement A then-undergraduate student identified only as Jane Doe made a complaint to campus police in November 2024, three weeks after the incident occurred, that she had been raped by a group of men at the Chi Phi fraternity house. She has filed a civil suit against the men and the university alleging that she had been drugged and raped. No criminal charges have been filed, but an investigation by the New York attorney general is ongoing. The case has rocked the university and started conversations about treatment of alleged sexual assault on college campuses across the country. James Knox, an attorney for Sarabia, argued that a gag order would limit "possible juror prejudice" and prevent the potential release of sensitive information that could lead to " threats, doxing, intimidation, and extrajudicial contact." Knox also submitted to the court a list of what he described as "prejudicial statements" made by Thomas Giuffra, an attorney for Jane Doe. Ryan Murphy/Getty Images - PHOTO: Student Isabel Breslin works on her laptop during a sit-in protest at Cornell University, Oct. 7, 2026, in Ithaca, N.Y. "Plaintiff's counsel has been trying his case in the media since filing the lawsuit," the motion alleged. "A full cataloguing of the media tour he has engaged in would be far lengthier than necessary to establish the potential risks these statements are incurring upon the fair administration of justice in this case and upon the parties." In a statement responding to the motion, Giuffra said, "The Defense has tried to rebut the claims in this case by engaging in a wholesale leaking of confidential documents, giving interviews calling Ms. Doe's story into question and calling her lawsuit immoral. These attempts to shift the narrative have not been successful." "The Defense is now attempting to silence me and Ms. Doe because we have been so successful in rebutting their ineffectual attempts to undermine her story," the statement said. "Truth always wins out." Sarabia is accused in the lawsuit of grabbing and kissing Jane Doe before "pouring lines of Ketamine all over her body and snorting them." He has denied wrongdoing, and according to Cornell documents reviewed by ABC News, he previously argued that the interaction was consensual. item.title: Bank of America hit with $1.2 billion penalty over money laundering failures
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Regulators fined Bank of America ( BAC ) more than $1.2 billion on Tuesday over widespread failures in the banking giant's safeguards against money laundering and other illicit financial activity. The Treasury Department said the nation's second-largest bank failed to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions and to report more than $5 billion in suspicious activity, including transactions potentially tied to Chinese money-laundering networks, narcotics trafficking, and fraud. The enforcement actions include a $1.2 billion penalty from the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), the third-largest fine in the Treasury Department's history after it fined crypto exchange Binance $3.4 billion in 2023 and TD Bank for $1.3 billion in 2024. The fine also includes a $750 million penalty from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the largest ever imposed by that regulator. The OCC penalty will be credited against FinCEN's assessment rather than added to it. Separately, a $11.6 million sanctions settlement brings the total penalties to more than $1.21 billion. "Even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. Bank of America's stock fell more than 2% after markets closed on Tuesday. It reports third quarter earnings Wednesday morning. The bank said it will include a "non-tax-deductible charge of $1.2 billion impacting net income by approximately 17 cents per share" in its third quarter results. "Financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right," a Bank of America spokesperson said in an email statement, adding that the Charlotte, North Carolina based lender has invested “billions of dollars in technology” and dedicated “thousands of employees to combat financial crime” to resolve the deficiencies. Regulators said Bank of America's failures extended across its transaction monitoring systems, customer due diligence, and internal oversight. The bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions, including over $1 billion involving national security-related and other priority illicit finance risks. FinCEN said Bank of America admitted to willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act and had effectively outsourced substantial portions of its suspicious activity detection responsibilities to law enforcement and other financial institutions. The bank also prioritized revenue over compliance resources, according to Treasury, allowing suspicious transactions to go uninvestigated for extended periods. The penalties come nearly two years after Bank of America agreed to a December 2024 cease-and-desist order requiring it to address longstanding weaknesses in its anti-money laundering controls. The OCC said the bank failed to make sufficient progress despite that earlier enforcement action. "Bank of America's poor response to its [Bank Secrecy Act] deficiencies is unacceptable," Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould said, describing continued breakdowns in internal controls. Separately, Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control announced an $11.6 million settlement involving 475 apparent violations of sanctions programs targeting Russia, Iran, and other countries and activities. As part of the latest enforcement actions, Bank of America must conduct a review of previously undetected suspicious transactions with an outside party and undergo independent assessments of its compliance controls. item.title: Apple's newest device is entering a market Amazon conquered years ago
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
After months of rumors, Apple is officially (and finally) making its biggest effort yet to grab a piece of the smart home pie. The iPhone maker announced the $299 HomeView on Tuesday, its first smart hub designed to put Siri front-and-center in people's homes. HomeView comes as a countertop device, or a slab you can mount to the wall, both with touchscreens, cameras and the ability to hear and execute Siri voice commands. This is Apple's first dedicated smart home hub ever, and it supports the numerous reports suggesting the company wants to make inroads in the home space. HomeView is designed to be stationary, and it not only connects all of your compatible devices together — things like smart lights, door locks and sensors (including the new Apple Home Collection ) — but also lets you control them using either the on-screen interface or Siri voice commands. But Apple may have a hard time convincing people to add yet another iPad-like screen to their homes, particularly one that emphasizes Siri. The new Siri, known as Siri AI , had a much delayed rollout and is only now available to users with the latest iPhones and devices running iOS 27 . Previously, Siri wasn't the most convenient voice assistant to use, nor the most helpful . Apple has a long way to go to catch up to the likes of Amazon's Alexa and Google's Assistant (now Gemini), and to make up for years of Siri being just meh. Plus, it's very late to the smart display party. To give credit where credit is due: Apple has certainly made progress with Siri. The new Siri AI is better at answering questions with greater detail than before, and it can include personal information from your calendar, Messages and other apps in its answers. This will likely come into play with the HomeView’s ability to recognize different users by their faces via the built-in camera and present personal information to them. But doing things that Alexa and Google have been able to do for a long time is just table stakes at this point. People barely want to use Siri on their iPhones; Apple not only has to prove Siri AI is good enough for people to want to use, period, but now it also has to show it's good enough to justify a separate, $299 device. With continuously skyrocketing tech prices , this may be a particularly tough sell. The fact that Apple is so late here is also working against the company. Amazon's original Echo Show came out in 2017, and Google's first Nest hub debuted in 2018. This isn't the first time Apple came into a space late of course — it has a habit of doing that and still coming out on top — but launching a device like this in 2026 feels a bit stale. Smart home hubs remain important for those building out connected spaces with dozens of devices, but plenty of smart home gear works over Wi-Fi now, no hub required. Privacy could be a selling point for HomeView, and it's an area where Apple has excelled in the past. Indeed, Apple is already emphasizing the privacy aspects of HomeView: the device runs on the A18 chip and includes Secure Enclaves, which are protected and compartmentalized, and process camera and microphone data. According to Apple, data processed by Secure Enclaves "cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple." Siri requests on HomeView can make use of on-device processing as well as Private Cloud Compute. Apple’s $299 HomeView is available for pre-order today, and will be widely available on November 13. item.title: Vatican says Pope Leo has lung cancer and the lower lobe of his right lung was removed
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
ROME (AP) — Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery Tuesday that confirmed that he has lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said. Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin after the surgery. It said the diagnosis had been suspected by preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery . The statement made no mention of treatment going forward, and the Vatican said doctors were not currently speaking of chemotherapy or other therapies pending the results of other tests. The Vatican press office noted the medical statement spoke of the “radical” removal of the lobe as an indication that doctors removed all suspect tissue in hopes of removing any lingering traces of the cancer. Leo's lymph nodes also would have been removed and tested, to determine if the cancer had spread, and there was no word yet on those test results. “Adenocarcinoma is the most common (type of lung cancer), also with the most favorable prognosis,” said Dr. Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center. “While we know the diagnosis we now need to know the stage." "We now need to know how big it is, how many spots in the lung are involved. Is it just one nodule, or more than one, and the lymph nodes, are they cancerous?” Liu said. If the cancer has spread, more tests will be needed to determine what kind of therapy to pursue, he said. Options include chemotherapy, a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy or targeted therapy, which involves oral pills for specific cancers. The Vatican says the surgery was successful The 71-year-old was in the operating room for about three hours, the statement said. The surgery itself lasted approximately 90 minutes. “The surgery was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement said, adding that the pope later returned to his room. Leo had walked into Rome’s Gemelli hospital through the main entrance earlier in the day and waved to dozens of well-wishers who had gathered to greet him. The Vatican said the surgery would be performed by a team led by Gemelli’s chief thoracic surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora. The American pontiff has offered a rare level of transparency about the first publicly disclosed major health problem of his 17-month papacy . He revealed the discovery of the localized nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed. Oncologists said prior to the operation that even if the nodule turned out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis would be “excellent” since it would have been removed at an early stage. The Vatican on Monday canceled all Leo’s audiences through Oct. 20. While Gemelli has a specific papal apartment that past popes have used, complete with a private chapel on the 10th floor, Leo will actually be staying in a nearby room since the papal apartment is undergoing renovations, according to the Vatican press office. Recovery could allow November travel to South America There was no word on whether Leo would be able to keep his planned trip to South America next month. Oncologists often advise patients not to fly for three weeks after surgery — which would give the pope just the interval needed to make his planned Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, depending on his recovery. The current itinerary for the trip is ambitious and the longest of his papacy to date, calling for Leo to clock just over 31,000 kilometers (19,000 miles) on a dozen flights and two helicopter rides, and a significant altitude change in Peru. "He has decided to undergo surgery soon in order to not change his plans for future overseas trips, so there is no need to worry, as it is not an emergency,” said Tokyo Cardinal Kikuchi Tsutomu, who saw Leo on Monday. A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters (1.2 inches) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended both to establish whether it is cancer and to treat a malignancy while it is still localized. Pope was hospitalized for typhoid fever in 1985 This is believed to be the second hospitalization for Leo, who is known to be sporty and in good shape, with weekly tennis games and swimming. As a young missionary priest, he came down with typhoid fever in 1985, soon after arriving in Chulucanas, Peru. The illness and hospitalization were a cathartic moment for him to decide to stay in the poverty and discomfort of Peru after living in relative comfort in Rome — a decision that ultimately paved the way to his papacy, according to an interview Leo gave to Elise Ann Allen in 2025 for “Pope Leo XIV: The Biography.” According to the book, Leo said he prayed to God to let him die rather than suffer the “horrible” pain of the fever. “I was hooked up to an IV, and I said, ‘If this is your sense of humor, Lord, I think you could do a little better.’ “Obviously, I survived; I recovered, but it turned out to be a very significant moment for me, because it was like, ’Well, you’ve already dealt with the illness; you already see what the needs are here — the order, the Augustinians, the church are telling you, ‘We need you here; go for it.’ I never looked back.” ___ Barry reported from Milan. ___ Associated Press religion coverage receives support through the AP’s collaboration with The Conversation US, with funding from Lilly Endowment Inc. item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes on Tuesday ordered a halt to tree-cutting at the East Potomac Golf Course until Oct. 26, putting a further pause on work at the historic D.C. course that has been part of President Donald Trump’s plans to remake the city . Reyes issued the order one day after a tense three-hour hearing in which she harshly criticized the government for having deceived her with its actions over the holiday weekend. At the Monday hearing, Reyes ordered a 24-hour pause that could be extended to 14 days if necessary. It was limited to one day while the government tried to find a key Trump administration official to discuss why a massive tree-cutting at the park needed to occur over the holiday weekend, with little notification to plaintiffs in a lawsuit trying to halt renovation plans or the judge. The judge also ordered during that period the government “must provide the court and plaintiffs three business days’ written advance notice prior to making any irreparable modification to any permanent form or feature of the East Potomac Golf Course.” The DC Preservation League and two local golfers are the plaintiffs in the lawsuit. The co-counsel in the case, Democracy Forward, thanked Reyes for stepping in and halting what the group called the “mad rush” to turn the public recreation space course into a high-end golf course. “We are pleased that the court intervened and will prevent additional work while we seek more lasting relief,” the group said in a statement. The Monday hearing and Tuesday order were prompted by the National Park Service ordering the cutting of hundreds of trees at the golf course after filing the court notification only minutes before the close of business on Oct. 9 on a holiday weekend, giving the plaintiffs little time to respond. At least 400 trees were cutdown over the weekend with plans for several hundred more. The historic park, especially the golf course, caught the eye of Trump, who wants to turn it into a world-class golf venue. It’s part of his grand vision for Washington, D.C., where he has multiple projects underway, including a $400 million White House ballroom and the soon-to-begin construction of his triumphal arch . He began talking about the city's public courses in late 2025. “When completed, this Course will have the ability to host Major Golf Tournaments, including The U.S. Open, The Ryder Cup, The PGA Championship, and other top PGA Tour events,” Trump posted on social media in June. The course has been the subject of multiple emergency hearings, including one in May in which Reyes was out of the country, because of concerns from the plaintiffs that the administration would move ahead with work despite the pending lawsuit. In each instance Reyes declined issuing temporary stop orders out of trust for the government's attorney in the case. “Every single time I have given the government the benefit of the doubt and every single time I made absolutely clear that I want notice,” Reyes said. “What has happened has cost the government all credibility with me.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/federal-judge-orders-trump-administration-170729125.html

Apple ( AAPL ) is reinventing its smart home strategy with its new HomeView hub, the HomePod Mini 2, and Apple TV 4K . Sporting a seven-inch Liquid Retina Display, the HomeView is designed to sit on a counter in its built-in speaker mount or be mounted to a wall. The $299 HomeView is designed to serve as the home base for your smart home and goes on sale Nov. 13. According to Apple, HomeView can recognize up to six household users via facial recognition and serve up their specific apps, notifications, and more. It can also play music and podcasts, make FaceTime calls, or look up quick video recipes in the kitchen. Users can control smart home devices ranging from lights and locks to thermostats and more, check their calendars, and interact with Siri AI to do things like find their keys via AirTags. Apple has dipped its toes into the smart home space over the years, including with the original HomePod, HomePod mini, and Apple TV, as well as software like its Home app, but has never offered a full-fledged hub like the HomeView before. Read more: 'I'm going to keep winning by innovating': Ring founder Jamie Siminoff isn't sweating Apple's smart home push Apple HomeView Apple Apple ceded much of the smart home space to rivals Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), which sell their Google Home and Amazon Alexa hardware lines. But the HomeView could change that. There are a number of do-it-yourself smart home options that allow users to set up a control center for their devices by mounting iPads on them. But the HomeView should provide a far easier, more cohesive offering for everyday consumers. Apple is also launching a new line of accessories built in collaboration with LG Electronics ( 066570.KS ) and Schneider. Called Apple Home Collection, the devices include a new LG in-home camera that can monitor your home and then turn the camera to face down when you enter the house for privacy. An outdoor camera can monitor deliveries and remember familiar faces. An LG door camera and lock can recognize your iPhone as you approach and quickly let you inside. Setting up the devices is as straightforward as connecting a pair of AirPods. Apple is marketing the Home Collection to individuals seeking products that easily integrate with the company's ecosystem and offer robust privacy features. The HomeView will be a major test for newly minted CEO John Ternus, who took over the top spot from Tim Cook on Sept. 1 and is reportedly angling to focus more on hardware and design. In addition to the HomeView, Apple also unveiled the $149 HomePod mini 2. Complete with new colors and Siri AI integration, the HomePod mini 2 allows you to do things like add events to your family calendar and ask about broad world knowledge. The $299 Apple TV 4K sports a more powerful processor and built-in far-field microphones that let you speak directly to the set-top box instead of holding down the remote's microphone button.
